content.comment_body: Hello AWS Community, AWS has updated its authorization policies, and as a result, the "AWSElasticBeanstalkFullAccess" policy is no longer available. Instead, you can add this authorization policy in IAM (Identity and Access Management) under Access Management > User: "[BINARY_DATA_REMOVED]" This change restores the ability to transfer [product_name] websites to AWS. The application example will be updated soon to reflect the new cloud connection process. Best regards, [user_name] Support

Hello, Unfortunately, the new process isn't working for me. I'm in sales and previously it worked perfectly with the AWSElasticBeanstalkFullAccess policy. Now, when I try to publish pages via [product_name] at Amazon, I encounter problems. Is there a waiting period after account creation before seamless uploading is possible?
Hello [user_name], Please refer to our workaround here: Workaround: Deploy the [product_name] project to AWS Best regards, [user_name] Support
Hello community, This workaround has been extended in this discussion: [product_name] / AWS missing permission Best regards, [user_name] Support

analysis.insight_summary: After AWS deprecated the "AWSElasticBeanstalkFullAccess" policy, users faced difficulties deploying [product_name] web projects to AWS, disrupting previously smooth workflows. The transition to the new access policy has caused authorization issues and impacted user satisfaction. Support has responded with workaround instructions and is updating guidance to help users through this transition phase, though some problems remain unsolved.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] project deployment to AWS to operate seamlessly and efficiently as it did previously. They look for clear, actionable support and an immediate solution to restore lost functionality.
